correctness.rationale: For an excluded translate of S, some barycentric lower threshold b_j is strictly above λ_j(y). Since the measure is supported on S, captured mass is at most P[λ_j>λ_j(y)]. Conversely b_j=λ_j(y)+ε and b_i=−b_j/d for the other facets realizes the corresponding one-coordinate cap, with atom-sensitive strict inequality; taking ε↓0 yields equality by continuity from below. Right-continuity of each CDF makes F_i(t)≥α exactly equivalent to t≥q_i(α). The sum-one barycentric constraint proves sum q_i≤1 iff feasible, and sorted sample coordinates give k*. Uniform-simplex Beta(1,d) marginals give unique barycentric center with depth 1-(d/(d+1))^d; opposite-facet-center atoms give sharp centerpoint 1/(d+1). Inspected source exact-rational verify.py independently enumerates feasible finite sample subsets; additional independent seven-query finite sample test reproduced the cap formula, not a proof for arbitrary measures.
